questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The interesting courses and beautiful city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great experience, but difficult to find - and expensive - housing

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very easily accessible on the English
uva.nl
homepage

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Practical information e-mails both before arrival and in the first weeks which were really helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was VERY difficult! I would recommend student to look several months if not more beforehand as not many are granted housing through the university. I found that
Kamernet.nl
was the best site for serious housing ads.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on-campus living as well as I am aware. But living off campus is great, the city is very young and international in pretty much every major area

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have loved more help on finding housing on your own. There really wasn't much help, there were some links on the university website but a lot of them were expired/faulty. Most trustworthy sites are in Dutch and some landlords will only take Dutch renters, so it would have been nice to be pointed in the right direction.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to find courses, but I would recommend students to only do courses in block 1 and 2 of the fall semester. The course calendar dates for block 3 is not respected at all. I had an exam date move to the end of February which couldn't be moved or anything to accommodate me, so I had to fly back in the middle of my semester at home.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course plans and dates were all on the university homepage and there were several emails with deadlines and other practical information about the registration process and which courses were offered for exchange students. You had to register the courses in GLASS, and that was easy as well - I ended up getting all of the courses that I had registered for

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not need help as there was a lot of information readily available, but I've heard that the study coordinators, etc. were always happy to help and easy to get in touch with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is pretty straightforward. I would suggest to read the course catalogue as it is very thorough and gives you a good idea of the workload and the themes covered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The teachers were incredibly inspiring and the academic environment was great.
The International Criminal law courses were twin courses and great, but their academic level was definitely the highest of the courses I took, and I was the only exchange student. The courses were part of a specific master's programme so everyone else knew each other and the teachers would often reference their other courses which I hadn't followed.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took MA courses even though I am a BA student and I did not find the course too challenging. The level of reading is high, but the overall academic level was not much different than what I am used to at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were a lot more lectures and also assignments which counted towards the final grade, which I really enjoyed. Also, the semester is divided into two or three parts so the courses are short and very intensive

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Human Rights law, Comparative law, International Criminal Tribunals - Procedural aspects, International Criminal Tribunals - substantive law, and International Environmental law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Human Rights law was a great course and the teacher was part of the UN Human Rights Committee so a lot of practical knowledge. Also, the course on Comparative law provided a lot of perspective on Western (Global North) law, so I would recommend it to all students from a Western law school

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I wouldn't call it unexpected per se, but I was surprised as to how expensive housing was. I ended up taking a ridiculously expensive room as I wouldn't have been able to go on exchange otherwise. The University said directly not to come if you did not have a rental contract.
The cost of housing definitely made me limit my spending on other items during my stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and transportation pretty much matched Denmark. I biked so that saved me a lot of money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The clubs (choir, art, sports, etc.) at the university all had really high entrance fees (500-1000 DKK) without counting activities on top, so I ended up not being able to afford being part of the university clubs.
Even the ones for e.g. board games and the exchange network had entrance fees so I opted to find my own friends instead

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different sports and art, singing, acting, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join whatever you'd like- but to know that it is quite expensive

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See Amsterdam - it is beautiful! But it is also really easy to get to other cities in the Netherlands which I did a lot. I also went to Belgium by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the Dutch are not that different from the Danes. However, they are difficult to talk to - but there are so many exchange students and international students doing their entire degree in the Netherlands so it is not a problem to find like-minded people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The locals were difficult - but international students were all very friendly. I would recommend joining a club if you are able. Otherwise, look at which courses have group projects; that's how I ended up making friends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch are very laid-back and enjoy going out for just a couple of beers and some games, etc. (but the night life in Amsterdam is amazing too, if that's what you're into) It was great fun.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find housing ASAP
2. Be sure to check the course calendars; but also be aware that exam dates may move. Do not take courses in block 3 as there is no guarantee that the exam will be held in January. I had two exam dates move - one of them was moved back a week only two days before we were supposed to take it and my exam date in block 3 was in the end of February even though the course itself ended in January.
3. Enjoy Amsterdam. It is a lovely city and it has so much to offer

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: enjoy your time there, it goes by fast!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience an international legal environment

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The living costs

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
